title: W5500 Ethernet Driver on TI C2000
description: Integrating a WIZnet W5500 Ethernet controller with the TI TMS320F28375D using SPI-B, FIFO and DMA transfers. The work focuses on a deterministic low-level driver and reliable Ethernet communication for an industrial controller.
details: Register-level SPI-B configuration with manual GPIO chip select and 8-bit W5500 SPI framing.
DMA transmit and receive path using CH5 for TX and CH6 for RX, with SPI FIFO coordination.
Driver API design around initialization, transfer, register read/write and socket operations.
Investigating intermittent communication failures, DMA peripheral interrupt flags and recovery behavior.
Using Wireshark, ping and Modbus polling to correlate firmware behavior with network traffic.
engineeringNotes: The observed CH6 PERINTFLG behavior during timeout conditions is a key debugging lead; clearing it manually was observed to restore transfers during testing.
The design preserves a register-level approach rather than relying on a high-level HAL.

title: Modbus TCP Communication for VFD
description: Industrial drive communication using a C2000 controller and W5500 Ethernet interface. The work includes initialization, socket management and repeated Modbus TCP register transactions with a PC-based Modbus client.
details: Configure W5500 network information and TCP server socket for Modbus TCP communication.
Exercise multiple-register reads using Modpoll and inspect transaction behavior.
Investigate long-run polling failures and socket state transitions.
Capture Ethernet traffic in Wireshark to distinguish protocol, socket and low-level driver faults.
engineeringNotes: A reported test ran thousands of transactions before the socket closed; subsequent reinitialization and reachability were investigated.
The project is a useful case study in long-duration communication testing and fault isolation.

title: DHCP Client with W5500
description: Developing a DHCP client flow for a W5500-based embedded Ethernet device so it can acquire network configuration dynamically rather than relying only on a static address.
details: Study DHCP Discover, Offer, Request and Acknowledge message sequence.
Construct and parse DHCP packets using the W5500 socket interface.
Extract offered IP address, subnet mask, gateway, DNS server and lease duration.
Inspect packet fields and transaction flow using Wireshark.
Focus on polling-based operation without SPI DMA or SPI interrupts for this implementation path.

title: Linux Mini Shell in C
description: A command-line shell project built in C to understand Linux process creation, command execution, built-in commands, signal handling and job control.
details: Build an interactive command loop and parse user-entered commands.
Execute external programs through fork/exec process APIs.
Implement required built-in command behavior and shell-side state handling.
Study foreground/background execution, signals and job-control behavior.
Compile with GCC warning and debug flags and resolve integration issues across source modules.

title: Modular Industrial IoT Gateway
description: A modular multi-node gateway concept for collecting sensor and machine data, bridging industrial field protocols and forwarding selected data to an IoT or supervisory system.
details: STM32 sensor node concept with MPU6050, air-quality sensing, RTC and OLED.
RP2040 peripheral node concept with RFID, servo and ultrasonic sensing.
ESP32 gateway concept with RS-485 master, CAN reception, BLE, Wi-Fi, MQTT and Ethernet.
Define message framing, node identity, data mapping and fault handling between nodes.
Plan incremental proof-of-concept stages before expanding to a Linux-based modular gateway.
engineeringNotes: This entry represents an architecture and project direction; individual modules should be marked complete only after hardware and firmware validation.

title: W55RP20 Industrial Ethernet Platform Evaluation
description: Evaluating the W55RP20-EVB-Pico as a compact Ethernet-enabled MCU platform for industrial communication firmware and update workflows.
details: Set up the WIZnet-PICO-C SDK and inspect its Pico SDK, ioLibrary and mbedTLS dependencies.
Investigate board-definition and CMake configuration issues for the W55RP20 EVB.
Assess EtherNet/IP adapter requirements, including explicit messaging and Class 1 I/O.
Review socket allocation, memory budget, RPI target and multiple scanner considerations.
Define an OTA maintenance state and safe firmware update sequence.
engineeringNotes: The EtherNet/IP commercial-stack port and complete adapter are planning/evaluation work, not claimed as a completed product implementation.

title: MicroShell on RP2040
description: A lightweight command interface built with the Raspberry Pi Pico SDK, providing a terminal-based way to interact with firmware and explore reusable command handling.
details: Configure and build the project using the Pico SDK toolchain.
Initialize stdio and USB terminal communication.
Build the ELF output and generate a UF2 image for board programming.
Explore extending shell commands to interact with I2C peripherals and an OLED display.

title: VFD Fleet API and Monitoring Architecture
description: Designing an API-only embedded HTTP interface for VFD products, intended to let a central dashboard read status and configure parameters without hosting a heavyweight web page on every drive.
details: Define JSON GET endpoints for status, parameters, active faults and fault history.
Define controlled POST endpoints for settings and commands.
Keep the existing register-level SPI-B DMA Ethernet driver as the network foundation.
Consider a compact device/session identity derived from a generated identifier and Modbus station ID.
Minimize CPU and RAM use by avoiding an embedded browser dashboard.
engineeringNotes: This is a product architecture direction. Do not describe the full API server as deployed until endpoint implementation and validation are complete.

title: EtherNet/IP Adapter Study for Industrial Controller
description: Researching an EtherNet/IP adapter implementation for a compact embedded industrial device, with a Rockwell CompactLogix scanner as the target PLC ecosystem.
details: Study the adapter role and CIP object model needed for a product device.
Evaluate explicit messaging and cyclic Class 1 I/O requirements.
Consider a 10 ms target RPI and multiple scanner connection behavior.
Plan socket usage, connection lifecycle, memory footprint and timing budget.
Compare commercial protocol stack integration and porting requirements for W55RP20.
engineeringNotes: This is a design and feasibility study; it is not represented as a certified EtherNet/IP implementation.

title: Embedded OTA and Secure Firmware Update Design
description: Exploring a robust firmware update architecture for industrial embedded controllers, including image integrity, authenticity, recovery and a known-good firmware image.
details: Separate download, validation and activation stages.
Evaluate packet-level CRC checks and whole-image CRC verification.
Study SHA-256 hashing and ECDSA signature verification for authenticity.
Plan inactive-image programming and rollback to a golden/known-good image.
Consider runtime flash integrity monitoring and safe maintenance mode.
engineeringNotes: The cryptographic boot and rollback flow is an architecture proposal and should not be presented as implemented without test evidence.

title: SPI FIFO and DMA Debugging on C2000
description: A focused firmware debugging investigation into the interaction between SPI FIFO thresholds, DMA burst/transfer configuration and peripheral interrupt flags on a TI C2000 device.
details: Inspect DMA channel configuration including burst size, burst count and transfer count.
Compare source/destination shadow address behavior with active address pointers.
Monitor SPI RX FIFO flags and DMA peripheral interrupt flags during normal and failed transfers.
Investigate why a pending receive peripheral event can stall subsequent transfers.
Build a repeatable diagnostic checklist for TX and RX DMA channels.

title: Dual-MCU ICU Syringe Pump Control Concept
description: A two-MCU syringe-pump architecture study separating the user interface from the real-time motor-control and sensing functions.
details: Low-cost STM32 UI/HMI concept with LCD, buttons, encoder and LVGL.
STM32G4 control MCU concept linked to the HMI over SPI.
Explore timer-driven step generation, DMA-backed communication buffers and safe command handoff.
Study plunger-position and syringe-profile based volume estimation.
Explore load-cell or strain-gauge force sensing for occlusion detection and NORMAL/WARNING/ALARM state handling.
engineeringNotes: This is a concept and engineering study, not a clinically validated medical device. Safety-critical medical use requires formal verification and regulatory processes.

title: ESP32 Home Automation and IoT Node
description: Exploring ESP32-based connected-device firmware and integration patterns, including ESPHome configuration and Home Assistant connectivity.
details: Work with ESP32-C6 development hardware and its GPIO/peripheral capabilities.
Configure ESPHome YAML for device behavior and network integration.
Understand device discovery, state reporting and Home Assistant entity mapping.
Use as a learning platform for embedded networking and connected product workflows.

title: WIZnet Ethernet Controller Evaluation
description: Comparing hardwired TCP/IP Ethernet controllers and Ethernet-capable MCU options for embedded products, with attention to interface, performance, resources and integration effort.
details: Evaluate W5500 and other WIZnet controller families for socket-based Ethernet.
Compare SPI-connected controllers with integrated MCU-plus-Ethernet options.
Consider CPU workload, memory, socket count, industrial temperature requirements and software ecosystem.
Match the hardware choice to application needs such as API server, Modbus TCP or EtherNet/IP.

title: Embedded MCU Development Board Laboratory
description: A hands-on development environment spanning microcontrollers and embedded platforms used to explore peripheral programming, firmware architecture, connectivity and toolchains.
details: Work across TI C2000, STM32, ESP32, RP2040/RP2350, CH32 and Nordic nRF52 platforms.
Use vendor IDEs and toolchains including Code Composer Studio, STM32 tools, MounRiver Studio, PlatformIO and Pico SDK.
Practice peripheral-level firmware, debugging, build systems and board bring-up.
Use this laboratory as a foundation for comparing MCU architectures and selecting hardware for industrial products.

title: Industrial Communication Protocol Research
description: A structured study of industrial communication protocols and their embedded implementation requirements, from serial fieldbus links to real-time Industrial Ethernet.
details: Study UART, SPI, I2C, RS-485 and Modbus RTU foundations.
Compare CAN and CAN FD communication and embedded integration.
Research EtherNet/IP adapter, EtherCAT and PROFINET device ecosystems.
Evaluate hardware, protocol stacks, RTOS/bare-metal tradeoffs and industrial temperature requirements.
Build practical implementation plans around MCU resources, timing and test equipment.

title: Embedded DSP and Motor-Control Learning Track
description: A planned hands-on track to build signal-processing and motor-control capability using STM32H7 and TI C2000 development platforms.
details: Plan ADC and DMA sampling with signal conditioning and anti-alias filtering.
Study moving-average, FIR, IIR, biquad and FFT-based analysis.
Explore harmonic and vibration analysis as signal-processing exercises.
Plan C2000 control experiments including PI loops, SVPWM and motor-control fundamentals.
Treat each item as a future lab exercise until a working prototype and measurements are available.

title: Linux Internals and Embedded Linux Practice
description: Building Linux systems knowledge relevant to embedded firmware engineering, including process control, shell development and future embedded Linux specialization.
details: Work through Linux process APIs, signals, command execution and job control.
Develop the Mini Shell as a practical systems-programming exercise.
Study Linux internals and command-line debugging workflows.
Plan progression toward device drivers, embedded Linux and Yocto-based product systems.
